questions.q: What was the Cold War, and how did it shape world politics?

answer.text: The Cold War was the period of intense rivalry and tension between the United States and its Western allies on one side and the Soviet Union and its Eastern allies on the other, lasting from the end of the Second World War until the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991. It was a war of ideology, between capitalism and communism, fought through an arms race, propaganda and competition for influence, but the two superpowers never fought each other directly, which is why it was called a cold war.

The Cold War divided the world into two blocs, making it bipolar. Rival military alliances such as NATO and the Warsaw Pact were formed. Crises like the Cuban Missile Crisis brought the world close to nuclear war, but the fear of mutual destruction acted as a deterrent. Many new nations, unwilling to join either bloc, formed the Non-Aligned Movement.

answer: Thus the Cold War dominated global politics for over four decades.

questions.q: What was the policy of Non-Alignment, and why did newly independent countries like India adopt it?

answer.text: was the policy of staying out of the two rival military blocs led by the United States and the Soviet Union during the Cold War.

list: Non-aligned countries refused to join either the American or the Soviet camp
They kept the freedom to judge each issue on its merits and to take independent decisions
Having just won freedom, they did not want to fall under the domination of any big power
It let them focus on their own development and keep peace, and gave them a collective voice in world affairs through the Non-Aligned Movement

questions.q: How did the Cuban Missile Crisis show the dangers of the Cold War?

answer.text: of 1962 was the moment the Cold War came closest to a nuclear war, revealing its terrible dangers.

list: The Soviet Union placed nuclear missiles in Cuba, close to the United States
The United States blockaded Cuba, and for days the world stood on the brink of nuclear conflict

answer.text: Both sides pulled back from the edge.

list: The crisis was resolved when the Soviets withdrew the missiles and the Americans promised not to invade Cuba
It showed how rivalry could threaten all humanity, and led both sides to seek ways to reduce the risk of war
